beginner.headline: Tomorrow (Mon Oct 12): conditional for beginners; lower confidence than a same-morning report, the morning on-site check decides. Long-period south swell holds Monday below advisory, easing slowly; Canoes was 2–3 ft+ (thigh to stomach, Surfline) this evening on a 16 s S swell. Lighter trades forecast, ENE about 7–10 kt. beginner.recommendation: Plan for 7–10:30 AM Monday: tide falling from the 5:04 AM high (2.2 ft) toward the 11:47 AM low (0.5 ft), so more water over the reef early, and trades at their lightest (NWS coastal waters: ENE 7–10 kt Monday; models about 7–8 kt early, building to about 10–11 kt late morning). Watch several full set cycles first: 16–18 s sets can run well above the 2–3 ft average and push further inside. One student or a small group of strong adults; several students or children only if sets stay manageable and drift is low. Brown, gray or cloudy water at Canoes or toward the Kūhiō drains / Ala Wai side ends it.

tide.rule: High tide is not automatically the best lesson time. Combine tide with swell, current, wind, water quality and the student.

current.multi_student: Lower tolerance: long-period sets can separate students. Only if drift is low and sets aren't reaching the inside.
